# Signed shape variations and a tied endpoint: an exact rate criterion

This is a local deformation theorem for three full-dimensional fibers
in arbitrary continuous dimension d>=1. It pays both source branches
when a signed variation can decrease total volume. It does not assert
existence of a favorable signed variation or of an attained extremizer.

## 1. Actual geometry and stated first-order hypotheses

Let A,K,B be convex bodies in R^d, with (A+B)/2 contained in K.
Their lifted convex hull at bases -1,0,1 has exactly these integer
fibers. Write a=|A|, k=|K|, b=|B|, M=a+k+b and r=Q/M. Assume
v_0,...,v_d span R^d with sole relation sum v_i=0. At y_0 in int K,
the caps whose B traces are supporting have common raw mass Q:

    h_i=h_B(v_i), beta_i=2v_i.y_0-h_i,
    |K intersect {v_i.x>=v_i.y_0}|
      +|A intersect {v_i.x>=beta_i}|=Q.

All A and K cuts are proper. Assume Q is the actual global maximum
raw mixed depth. The ordinary raw endpoint maxima satisfy

    m_A<Q, m_B=Q.

Let A_t,K_t be actual convex bodies for 0<=t<t_0, with A_0=A,
K_0=K and (A_t+B)/2 contained in K_t. Assume Hausdorff convergence,
|A_t triangle A|+|K_t triangle K|=O(t), and

    |A_t|+|K_t|=a+k+tD+o(t).                         (1)

Here triangle denotes symmetric difference; D may have either sign.
Put s_i^0=v_i.y_0. Require the following uniform first variation,
for each fixed R and |s-s_i^0|<=Rt:

    |K_t intersect {v_i.x>=s}|
       +|A_t intersect {v_i.x>=2s-h_i}|
      =Q-s_i(s-s_i^0)+t eta_i+o(t),                (2)

where s_i=k_i+2sigma_i, k_i and sigma_i are the original normalized
proper-section measures of K and A respectively. Thus k_i,sigma_i>0.
The symbols s_i and s_i^0 have distinct meanings: the former is a
section coefficient, the latter a scalar projection. Let

    lambda_i=1/s_i, Lambda=sum lambda_i,
    q_shape=sum lambda_i eta_i/Lambda,
    C=q_shape-rD.                                  (3)

These are explicit hypotheses satisfied by the audited polygonal
face changes, including the signed facet path when its geometric
construction and first variation are established. No regularity of
an arbitrary unstated body path is presumed.

## 2. A second actual motion preserves compatibility

Fix q in B and v>=0. In addition to the given shape path contract B:

    B_t=q+(1-vt)(B-q).

For small t this is nested in B, so (A_t+B_t)/2 remains contained in
K_t. Its support value is h_i-tv e_i, e_i=h_i-v_i.q>=0. Consequently
the A threshold of its supporting cap becomes 2s-h_i+tv e_i.
The cap perturbation from this extra threshold shift is

    -tv sigma_i e_i+o(t).                          (4)

Here (4) follows from Hausdorff convergence of convex A_t and the
properness of the limiting slice. For clarity, sections at scalar
heights tending to beta_i converge in Hausdorff distance to the
proper section of A, after identification of parallel planes. Upper
inclusion follows by compactness. Lower inclusion follows by mixing
each point of the limiting section with points in interior balls
strictly on either side and using eventual interior containment under
convex Hausdorff convergence. Their (d-1)-volumes therefore converge.
Integrating these section measures over the length-O(t) interval
proves (4) uniformly at |s-s_i^0|=O(t). This also covers d=1, where
the proper section density is the fixed normalized counting measure.

Thus the new cap budget has expansion (2) with eta_i replaced by
eta_i-v sigma_i e_i. Define

    J(q)=sum lambda_i sigma_i(h_i-v_i.q)/Lambda>=0. (5)

The new total mass is M+t(D-dbv)+o(t).

## 3. One actual meeting point and the all-source upper bound

Each new scalar cap-budget function is continuous and strictly
decreasing near s_i^0. The K_t slices provide a uniform positive
lower bound on its decrease, because a fixed ball around y_0 lies
in all K_t for small t. Compact common bounding balls provide uniform
upper section bounds. The symmetric-difference hypothesis and the
support shift imply a uniform O(t) difference from the original
budget functions.

Their local inverse projection levels at a common budget u are
continuous and strictly decreasing in u. Summing these levels gives
a strictly decreasing scalar function. At the two ends of a fixed
small interval about Q it has opposite signs, since it does at t=0.
It has a unique zero, and the two-sided slope bounds give a common
budget Q_t=Q+O(t) and levels s_i(t)=s_i^0+O(t). The sum-zero vector
of levels determines one actual y_t=y_0+O(t) in int K_t, since the
normals identify R^d with the coordinate sum-zero subspace.

Expansion (2), together with (4), now gives

    Q_t=Q+t(q_shape-vJ(q))+o(t).                    (6)

To verify the derivative, any subsequential limit of the bounded
difference quotients satisfies the linear cap equations. Multiplying
them by lambda_i and summing cancels the source motion. This fixes
the common-budget derivative as in (6); the spanning normals then
fix the source derivative. Uniqueness gives convergence of every
difference quotient.

The new middle halfspaces cover all of R^d since sum v_i=0. Their
common budget therefore bounds every middle-fiber depth. B's exact
ordinary maximum is (1-vt)^d Q. A_t's ordinary maximum is at most
m_A+|A_t triangle A| and retains a strict gap. For this last
inequality one may take the supremum over all points in R^d: the
ordinary depth of a point outside a compact convex body is zero
by strict separation, and each halfspace measure changes by at most
the symmetric-difference volume. This accounts for new points in A_t.

At either extreme integer level, the ordinary endpoint depth equals
the mixed depth, since a sufficiently steep finite integer tilt
isolates the endpoint for any prescribed continuous cap. Hence the
actual new global maximum is bounded by the maximum of (6), the
contracted B maximum, and the still-gapped A maximum.

## 4. Exact feasibility of strict decrease of both active branches

After division by the true new total mass, the menu derivative has
sign determined by

    C+v(drb-J(q)),                                 (7)

and the tied endpoint derivative has sign determined by

    -r[D+dv(a+k)].                                 (8)

For (8), expand -dvQ-r(D-dbv) and use Q-rb=r(a+k).
Thus this particular upper certificate strictly decreases to first
order exactly when

    C+v(drb-J(q))<0,    D+dv(a+k)>0.               (9)

Let

    v_0=max{0,-D/[d(a+k)]}.

If D>0 the endpoint condition permits v=0; otherwise it requires
v>v_0. An affine function of v is negative at some permitted v if
and only if

    J(q)>drb  OR  C+v_0(drb-J(q))<0.              (10)

Indeed, a negative slope makes it negative for a sufficiently large
finite v. With nonnegative slope its smallest value is the value at
the lower endpoint; strict negativity there is necessary, and by
continuity sufficient even when that endpoint is excluded.

When D<0, the second alternative is equivalently

    d(a+k)q_shape+D J(q)-dQD<0.                   (11)

This follows by multiplying the boundary value by d(a+k) and using
rM=Q. When D>=0 it is simply C<0. In particular a negative menu
cost alone does NOT suffice if a tied endpoint survives a total-mass
decrease; equation (11) records the missing payment exactly.

## 5. The contraction center can be selected by one support function

All section weights in this proper-cut result are fixed. Put

    V=sum lambda_i sigma_i v_i.

Then

    J_max=[sum lambda_i sigma_i h_i+h_B(-V)]/Lambda. (12)

This maximum is attained by one actual q in B, by compactness.
Both alternatives in (10) are monotone in J, because v_0>=0.
Consequently there exist an actual contraction center and a finite
rate giving the strict two-branch decrease if and only if (10)
holds with J_max. The support point in (12) supplies that center.
The case V=0 is harmless: every q attains the same value.

All statements above concern this specified local certificate. Failure
of (10) does not rule out another body deformation, higher-order
descent, or a different proof mechanism. No automatic positivity of
D, negativity of C, or sufficient support payment is claimed.
